subject: A Level Biology
title: Oxygen dissociation curves
question:
Fig. 7.1 shows the oxygen dissociation curves for haemoglobin at two different partial pressures of carbon dioxide.
(a) State the percentage saturation of haemoglobin at 4 kPa for curve A.
(b) Explain why curve B is to the right of curve A.
(c) Suggest how this shift helps respiring muscle tissue.

scene: Both curves come from the same S shaped formula. Curve B uses a higher half saturation point, which shifts it to the right.

figure:
A graph on a grid. Horizontal axis: partial pressure of oxygen / kPa, from 0 to 14, marked every 2. Vertical axis: saturation of haemoglobin / %, from 0 to 100, marked every 20.
Two S shaped oxygen dissociation curves, both rising from near 0 and levelling off near 100 %.
Curve A, solid, reaches 50 % at about 3.5 kPa. Curve B, dashed, is shifted to the right and reaches 50 % at about 4.8 kPa.
Label the curves A and B.
Caption: Fig. 7.1.
